subject: Nariway Signals - 2026-08-26 - the anti-museum, and a museum's core redefined
html:
Nariway Signals
Wednesday, August 26, 2026
Heaviest today on the honest spread between keeping, giving, and selling — a Denver collector publicly rejecting the vanity-museum model just as one of DC’s oldest house-museums finally settles an 18-month fight over what its own founder’s “core collection” even means, with a first-ever tribal repatriation and a total, cheerfully specific collection dispersal as further points on the same spectrum.
Lead
A Denver collector built the anti-museum, and made the case for it in print
Elisa Carollo’s Aug 25 Observer profile lays out what Amanda Precourt actually built: a condemned fortune-cookie factory in Denver’s Baker neighborhood, turned into Cookie Factory, a free 5,000+ sq ft public art space — exhibition and studio rooms, a video/sound theater, a sculpture garden — self-funded, artistic director Jérôme Sans, opened May 2025. She lives above it with her own collection. What makes it a lead rather than a footnote is the framing: this brief has spent weeks tracking collectors who build mega-museums under their own names as the default legacy vehicle — Lucas, Costantini at Malba, van Caldenborgh at Voorlinden, Rosenkranz at Canyon. Precourt is a living collector publicly arguing for the opposite, access and artist commissions over a founder’s monument, in the same week this brief also logs a museum fighting over what “core” even means once a founder is gone.

Art Spell roundup →
What’s happening
The Phillips Collection has ended an 18-month fight over what its founder’s “core collection” actually is
Washington’s Phillips Collection — pressing ahead with a plan to sell works by Georgia O’Keeffe, Georges Seurat, and Anish Kapoor at Sotheby’s since 2024 — has reached an agreement with its board of members (including Phillips family descendants and former staff) redefining “core collection” to cover the full 1985 catalogue, not the narrower 1999 list the museum had used since 2000. The ten contested works can now be sold; everything else in the broader catalogue is now permanently protected. A quieter cousin of the Ty Warner donor-intent fight already tracked here: who gets to define a founder’s collection decades after the founder is gone, resolved this time by redrawing the boundary rather than litigating it.
Artnet →
A Cisco co-founder’s three-decade cat-art collection is being fully dispersed at Bonhams
Sandy Lerner’s collection — “one of the most significant private collections of cat-related decorative arts, books, and collectibles ever assembled,” the subject of her own 2017 book Caticons — goes to auction in two parts: online Sept 22–Oct 1, and live Sept 30 at Bonhams’ new New York flagship, 66 lots including a Foujita and a Giacometti. No foundation, no museum, just a clean, cheerfully specific instance of the plain “sell” pathway — this year’s third major single-owner dispersal alongside Lust and Blaquier.
ARTnews →
The Speed Art Museum completed its first-ever NAGPRA repatriation
On Aug 19, the Louisville museum returned 24 sacred and cultural items — a sundance rattle, a beaded turtle amulet, a pipe bag, moccasins, a Cheyenne cradle board — to the Southern Cheyenne and Arapaho tribes, after three years of consultation. The items had sat in the collection since 1930, gifted by a German-American ethnographer. A clean positive counterpart to Monday’s lead about Canada’s federal Indigenous Art Centre losing track of 111 works: this is what deliberate stewardship looks like when an institution actually owns the file.
ARTnews →
Worth reading
Tatum Dooley, “Ep 10: We Answer Your DMs” (Art Forecast, Aug 19)
A lighter-format, DM-answering episode that still lands squarely on Nariway’s terrain — artists copying themselves, trust between artists and collectors, and, the phrase worth flagging, “collecting as autobiography.” Close enough to Nariway’s own Artobiography thesis to be worth a listen even in podcast form.
Art Forecast →
To see
Christie’s Alan Medaugh Hiroshige preview is now 16 days out
Public preview Sept 11–14, sale Sept 15, 20 Rockefeller Plaza — already on the calendar for the Sept 12 preview.
ARTnews →
Sotheby’s Open House (Sept 20–21) is now inside a month out
Its confirmed program includes a session on legal considerations across an art collection’s lifecycle, staged by the house’s own trusts-and-estates practice — a rare instance of a major auction house running the succession conversation in public.
Sotheby’s →
For the record
Phoenix Art Museum’s The Way We Came opened yesterday, Aug 26
Closing the loop on the escalation tracked here all week. Built on the 185-work William P. Healey Collection gift, the largest gift of Native American art in the museum’s 65-year history; runs through Jul 11, 2027.
